svg.aria-label: Partial hydrogenation of a vegetable oil. Top: a liquid triglyceride, a glycerol backbone with three ester-linked 18-carbon chains: two linoleate chains with two C=C double bonds each and one oleate chain with one C=C. Adding 3 H2 with a nickel catalyst and heat saturates some of the double bonds. Bottom: a partially hydrogenated, soft solid fat with two oleate chains and one fully saturated stearate chain. Fewer double bonds make straighter chains that pack together; partial hydrogenation can also convert some cis double bonds to trans.

svg.text: Partial hydrogenation of a vegetable oil
Vegetable oil (liquid): a triglyceride with unsaturated chains
H2​ adds across some C=C bonds
Partially hydrogenated oil (soft solid, e.g. margarine)
Fewer C=C double bonds = straighter chains that pack together, so the fat is more solid.
The highlighted C=C bonds are the ones that react. Partial hydrogenation can also flip some
cis C=C bonds to trans, which is where trans fats come from.
